# Authenticated broker qualification — 2026-11-18

The authenticated task broker is deployed on host-a at
`https://192.0.2.10:19443`, supervised by `lit-task-broker.service` under a
separate non-login account. Worker publication and merge admission go through
individual mTLS identities and durable assignment capabilities. The broker alone
holds the sandbox GitHub write credential. This is a qualified three-host pilot,
not yet a 100-agent authenticated broker load qualification.

Implementation is on `codex/mit-lit-recovery`, based on MIT snapshot
`98c59bb2dbebcf7f575993a4ad89e1300a578c83` and independently authored recovery
changes. No post-MIT upstream Lit implementation was used; v1.8.0 remained a black
box and was not invoked for this deployment. The parent before this commit was
`6159a48b949167f5304b276c740e98cddfcc123f`; its separate provenance documentation
change was preserved.

## Enforcement and deployment

The repository-selected broker App is `100latent-lit-task-broker` (App 5812726,
installation 183217509). Its only write permissions are Contents and Pull requests;
Actions, Checks, Administration and Metadata are read-only. The three old worker
App installations (183007293, 183007312, 183007323) are suspended. Their actual
previous credentials were rejected on host-a, host-e and host-f with HTTP 403 and an
explicit suspended-installation response. Replacement broker-issued tokens can
read the private repository, but cannot create refs, use asynchronous merge, or
invoke GraphQL `enqueuePullRequest`: all three hosts received permission denials,
including GraphQL `FORBIDDEN`, rather than merely a closed-PR validation error.

The original main ruleset 27439049 is unchanged: no bypass actors, native GitHub
Actions App 15368 provenance, required PRs and native merge queue. No manual commit
statuses were created. Original worker ownership rules remain unchanged. Broker
proposal namespace rule 27531243 permits only the broker Integration; freeze rule
27529010 prohibits updates/deletions of exact enrolled refs, with no bypasses.
The catch-all creation rule excludes the separately protected broker namespace.

An attempted extra main-update restriction was rejected as a deployment design:
`always` bypass blocked admission; `exempt` admitted entries but blocked GitHub's
native merge executor after checks passed. A bot-user exemption also failed. That
experimental rule (27528579) was removed after worker-writer suspension. Its failed
rule-suite and admission evidence remains in the raw evidence directory. Credential
separation, not that extra rule, is the final enforcement boundary.

A separate read-only observer runs in the operator's Mac login session. It supplies
filtered policy/installation metadata because App ruleset reads omit bypass actors.
Its GitHub credential stays on the Mac. Observations expire within 30 seconds;
mutations fail closed without a fresh observation or when retired writers are
reactivated. A live expiry control held an eligible PR unqueued until observation
resumed before the final credential cutover; final-adapter expiry and revocation
behavior is also covered by native regressions. Already admitted GitHub entries
can complete independently of the broker or observer.

Deployed source hashes matched the qualified sources after restart. The service
is enabled and active; authenticated health and persisted-state reconciliation
were checked. A distinct co-hosted worker UID cannot read broker keys/authority
or modify deployed code. host-e and host-f clients run under the existing lab login;
this does not qualify arbitrary untrusted processes sharing that account. All
privileged host and GitHub policy operators remain trusted.

Private staging keys, raw token files and raw claim-capability receipts were
removed or replaced by redacted receipts with original-record hashes. Only the
deployed broker signing key remains registered (fingerprint
`SHA256:juJoBHKsac6Jgu1wg2R4IecOBPN2CTovMK7+ioxPQGs=`). Intended private operator
CA/client profiles and host-local credentials remain in private directories.

## Live reassignment and Actions evidence

After write-credential cutover, host-a published PR
[#108](https://github.com/100latent/lit-merge-queue-sandbox/pull/108) through the
broker. The scheduler froze its ref, it passed automatic preflight and entered the
queue. Reassignment to host-e revoked the old capability, withdrew and closed #108,
and withheld the successor capability while the previous attempt drained. Stale
submission stayed rejected. The successor was also published through the broker:
[#109](https://github.com/100latent/lit-merge-queue-sandbox/pull/109) merged as
`d021d9f8a86287da0a41ff230f96172a32a288d2`.
Its [native merge-group run](https://github.com/100latent/lit-merge-queue-sandbox/actions/runs/44266130739)
checked that exact landed commit with App 15368. Completed publication replay after
restart returned the existing receipt without another PR.

Earlier worker-authored pilot successors #104 and #107 also merged; rejected or
retired #103, #105, #106 and #108 did not. #106 exposed a real preflight-selection
bug: an older success at the same SHA could obscure a newer pending run. The
coordinator now requires the newest relevant native workflow to finish successfully.
Unknown enqueue outcomes are never blindly retried. A scheduler-only recovery API
consumes one verified native branch-protection removal event before retry eligibility;
it cannot reset an unknown pending RPC or reuse an old receipt.

Native Git fetched the sandbox with a broker-issued read-only token. Strict full
`git fsck` passed. The merged successors are ancestors of main; retired heads are
not. Exact successor file content is present and the retired attempts' files are
absent. All registered proposals ended merged or ownership-retired.

## Test scope

| Platform | Coordinator | Broker | Result |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| Local macOS arm64 | 41 | 21 | Passed |
| host-a Linux x86_64 | 41 | 21 | Passed |
| host-e Linux arm64 | 41 | 21 | Passed |
| host-f Linux arm64 | 41 | 21 | Passed |

Coverage includes stale/competing claims, authenticated roles, revoked writers,
policy expiry/mismatch, capability fencing, immutable broker receipts, publication
idempotency and unknown effects, attempt-scoped request IDs, read-only tokens,
certificate removal, request/path limits and safe confirmed-removal recovery.
Two initial host runs encountered legitimate busy responses in positive test
clients. Those clients now retry the identical idempotent request; adversarial
and competing-claim tests retain first-response observations. Failed-run logs and
the earlier source archive are preserved. All final four-platform runs passed.

The complete local Rust suite passed: 486 test executions across Cargo targets,
using `cargo test --locked -- --test-threads=1`, including crash/concurrent-writer
regressions. Nested child-process test summaries are excluded from that total.
The full Rust suite was not rerun on Linux in this task. Rust source is unchanged.

Live sandbox Actions checked its existing batch regressions and 10/50/100-worker
fixtures on exact integration candidates, with zero manual statuses. Those are
not 100 authenticated live broker agents. The new Python suites ran natively on
all four platforms; recovery-branch workflow changes have not yet run remotely.

## Remaining work and operational limits

- Run a real 25–100-agent burst through broker publication and reassignment,
  including overlapping edits, load, API limits and interruptions.
- Extend the current 32-file/64-KiB regular UTF-8 add/update publication API if
  binary files, deletes, mode changes or full Git object upload are needed.
- Add automated reconciliation/cleanup for unknown unregistered publications,
  which can leave orphan refs/PRs; genuinely unobservable close requires an operator.
- Qualify availability and renewal: one broker host, one Mac login-session observer,
  30-day leaf certificates, and manual exact-ref freezing by the trusted scheduler.
- Continue scheduler dependency/overlap hints and remaining prioritized parity.
  Do not restore worker write credentials while claiming broker-only enforcement.
